q: A release of an agile product has just shipped, but the project continues for another year. Does Close Project or Phase apply now?
options: No, it applies only at the very end of the project
Yes, it applies to releases and iterations too
Only if the release failed its acceptance
Only for the contracts used in the release
explanation: Close Project or Phase finalizes activities for projects, phases, releases, iterations or contracts. In adaptive approaches it centers on wrapping up the release or iteration.

q: The final deliverable is accepted, but two supplier invoices are still being booked to another cost center. What must happen before the project accounts are closed?
explanation: Exit criteria include verifying that all costs have been charged to the project, then closing project accounts.
options: Nothing, since closure can go ahead as soon as it is accepted
Ask finance to write off the invoices
Leave the project accounts open for a year
Make sure all costs are charged to the project

q: Before a new system is handed to operations, what does a transition readiness assessment check?
options: The organization's ability and interest to use it
The development team's velocity in the last iteration
The vendor's payment history
The number of change requests raised
explanation: A readiness assessment determines the ability and interest of the organization to transition to the future state, and identifies gaps in readiness as risks, with responses.
ref: The PMI Guide to Business Analysis, 5.5.3.1

links.label: The PMI Guide to Business Analysis, 5.5.3.1

q: The readiness assessment finds that the service desk has not been trained on the new system. Where should the response be planned?
options: In the risk register only, as an accepted risk
In the lessons learned register
In the transition plan, with training
In the final report, as a variance
explanation: The transition plan builds on the readiness assessment and includes operational procedures, training collateral, service-level agreements, rollout material and contingency plans.
ref: The PMI Guide to Business Analysis, 5.5.3.2

links.label: The PMI Guide to Business Analysis, 5.5.3.2

q: In an adaptive project with small, frequent releases, how might transition work be planned, according to the business analysis guide?
options: Only as a separate formal plan after the very last release
As transition stories, or in the definition of done
It is not needed in adaptive projects
By the sponsor alone, after closure
explanation: For small incremental releases, there are transition tasks in a story or separate transition stories; transition may also be part of the definition of done, or a reserved block of time or iteration.
ref: The PMI Guide to Business Analysis, 5.5.4

links.label: The PMI Guide to Business Analysis, 5.5.4

q: At closure, a risk that the new system may fail under peak load is still open. What should the project manager do?
options: Delete it, as the project is ending
Keep it in the archived project file only
Wait for it to happen before acting
Accept it or transition it to operations
explanation: Close Project or Phase identifies outstanding risks that should be accepted or transitioned to operations.

q: The supplier's work is accepted, but its warranty claim on one component is still open. What must happen before the contract is closed?
options: Finalize the claim and any warranties
Close the contract and leave the claim
Pass the claim on to the next project
Cancel the warranty to speed up closure
explanation: Contract completion includes confirming formal acceptance, finalizing open claims, guarantees and warranties, updating records, paying all invoices and archiving information.

q: Who gives the seller formal written notice that the contract has been completed?
options: The lead developer on the project team
The seller's own account manager
The buyer's procurement administrator
The sponsor of the next project
explanation: The buyer, usually through its authorized procurement administrator, provides the seller with formal written notice that the contract has been completed.

q: At closure, only half of the planned benefits have appeared so far. What should the final report say about them?
explanation: If the benefits are not met at the close of the project, the final report indicates the degree to which they were achieved and an estimate for future benefits realization.
options: That benefits are not the project's concern at all
The degree achieved and an estimate for the rest
Nothing, as benefits are reported later
That the project failed completely

q: After the project closes, who is accountable for monitoring, recording and reporting the realized benefits?
options: The project's lead tester
The procurement administrator
The scrum master
The benefits owner
explanation: The benefits management plan names a benefits owner: the person accountable for monitoring, recording and reporting realized benefits throughout the timeframe established in the plan.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 4, Benefits management plan

links.label: PMBOK 8, Guide section 4, Benefits management plan

q: The PMBOK Guide adds one closure procedure for projects that may end before completion. What is it?
options: Investigating and documenting why it ended
Skipping closure, as nothing was delivered
Transferring the team at once without records
Keeping the budget open in case it restarts
explanation: The process includes establishing procedures to investigate and document the reasons a project may have been terminated before completion.

q: Which of these belongs in the final report?
options: The team's personal performance ratings
The detailed daily task list
Reasons for cost and schedule variances
The vendor's internal cost data
explanation: The final report summarizes performance: scope, quality, cost and schedule objectives with actual results and reasons for variances, validation of the result, benefits and business needs met, and risks and issues.

q: Closure is near, and the project still holds rented test equipment until the end of the month. What should the project manager do?
explanation: Exit criteria include reallocating or releasing project facilities, equipment and other resources, and addressing excess materials.
options: Keep it in case some new project needs it later
Release it so it stops charging the project
Give it to a team member to keep
Wait for operations to request it

q: Two developers leave next week for another project, before closure is finished. What should happen before they go?
explanation: Closure includes managing knowledge sharing and transfer and documenting lessons learned, before personnel are reassigned or released.
options: Nothing, as they can leave at any time
They should first rewrite all of the project documentation
Their access should stay open indefinitely
Their knowledge should be shared and recorded

q: At the close of a two-year project, the lessons learned register holds only three entries, all written in the last week. What went wrong?
options: It should have been updated throughout
It should be written only at closure
Lessons are not needed for successful projects
Only the sponsor may add lessons
explanation: The lessons learned register is created early in the project and then used and updated in many processes throughout, by the people involved in the work.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 4, Lessons learned register

links.label: PMBOK 8, Guide section 4, Lessons learned register

q: At closure, the team has ideas to improve the company's change control procedure. What should happen to them?
explanation: Closure collects suggestions for improving or updating organizational policies and procedures and forwards them to the appropriate unit; outputs include organizational process asset updates.
options: Keep them in the team's private chat channel for later
Apply them to the project that is closing
Forward them to the unit that owns the procedure
Discard them, as the project is over

q: An agile team finishes a release. What does closing the release include, according to the PMBOK Guide?
explanation: In adaptive approaches, closure includes knowledge-sharing sessions and retrospectives on the iteration or release, and a discussion of outstanding risks.
options: Rewriting the original project charter
A retrospective and knowledge-sharing sessions
Freezing the backlog for the next year
Removing the product owner from the team at once

q: Before an iteration is closed, what must the team confirm?
options: The burndown reached zero on the last day
The sponsor attended every daily meeting
All change requests were rejected
Prioritized items are done and accepted
explanation: Completing a release or iteration means confirming that prioritized backlog items are finished, acceptance criteria are met, and deliverables are reviewed and accepted by stakeholders.

q: Closure must verify obligations beyond the contract. Which set does the PMBOK Guide name?
options: Contractual, regulatory, legal, social and environmental
Only those signed by the sponsor
Only the internal quality checklist
Only those the customer complains about
explanation: Additional closure activities include verifying that all contractual, regulatory, legal, social and environmental obligations have been met, and measuring stakeholder satisfaction.

q: Why should the stakeholder who will approve the deliverables be involved early in the project?
options: So that formal closure can be skipped
To replace the project's quality team
To give feedback on quality along the way
To sign the charter instead of the sponsor
explanation: The authorized stakeholder who approves the deliverables should be involved early and give feedback on their quality, so the team can assess quality and recommend changes.

q: What is the purpose of the final product, service or result transition?
options: To restart the whole project in a new phase
To hand the result to the group that will run it
To return all the unused budget to the sponsor
To record the team's lessons learned
explanation: Once delivered, the product, service or result may be handed over to a different group or organization that will operate, maintain and support it; at phase end, the intermediate result goes to the next phase.
ref: PMBOK 8, Guide section 4, Final product, service, or result transition

links.label: PMBOK 8, Guide section 4, Final product, service, or result transition

q: Which data analysis techniques does the Close Project or Phase process use?
options: Earned value analysis and make-or-buy analysis
Pareto charts and fishbone diagrams
Planning poker and affinity grouping
Document, regression, trend and variance analysis
explanation: Figure 2-12 lists expert judgment, data analysis (document, regression, trend and variance analysis) and meetings.

q: What should the project manager do before handing the app to the operations team?
options: Hand it over now, since operations can learn on the job
Assess readiness and plan training and support hours
Keep the app with the project team for a year
Ask the vendor to run operations instead
explanation: Validating readiness for transition comes first: a readiness assessment finds the gaps (no training, no agreed support hours), and the transition plan covers training, service levels and contingency.
ref: The PMI Guide to Business Analysis, 5.5

links.label: The PMI Guide to Business Analysis, 5.5

q: What must happen with the vendor before its contract is closed?
options: Settle the open claim and pay the final invoice
Close the contract now, since the claim can wait
Withhold payment until the claim is dropped
Refer the claim to court at once
explanation: Contract completion requires finalizing open claims, paying all invoices due to external sources, updating records and archiving. Negotiation is the preferred way to settle the claim; court is the last option.

q: Which document will summarize whether the app met the library's business needs and how the open issues were handled?
options: The team charter
The issue log
The final report
The risk register
explanation: The final report summarizes project performance, including how the result achieved the business needs and the risks or issues encountered and how they were addressed.

q: Which THREE are exit criteria for closing a predictive project?
options: Deliverables formally accepted by the customer
All costs charged to the project
Project personnel reassigned or released
A new project charter approved
The backlog frozen for a year
All lessons deleted after the final report
explanation: Exit criteria include updated documents and resolved issues, value delivered with a plan to maintain it, formal acceptance, costs charged, accounts closed, people and resources released, and final reports prepared.

q: Which TWO does a transition plan cover, according to the business analysis guide?
options: Training material for the users
Contingency plans for the rollout
The project charter
The bidder conference minutes
The team's velocity history
explanation: Transition planning includes information to support operational procedures, training collateral, service-level agreements, rollout collateral, coordination with other releases and contingency plans.
ref: The PMI Guide to Business Analysis, 5.5.4

links.label: The PMI Guide to Business Analysis, 5.5.4

q: Which TWO happen when an adaptive release is closed?
options: A retrospective on the release
Open risks moved to later releases or operations
A new business case for every story
Freezing all future backlog changes
Rebaselining the critical path
explanation: Adaptive closure includes retrospectives and knowledge sharing, and discussing outstanding risks to accept or transition to later iterations, releases, clients and operations.

q: Match each closure area with its activity.
right: Settle claims and pay all invoices
Charge all costs and close the accounts
Document lessons learned and archive records
explanation: These are the closing activities the outline names: final lessons learned and retrospectives, procurement, financials and resources.

q: Complete each statement about closure.

blanks.text: Checking the organization's ability and interest to adopt the result is a
Formal written notice that a contract is complete is given by the
Records and lessons kept for future projects are

explanation: Readiness is checked before transition; the buyer closes the contract formally; archived knowledge updates the organizational process assets.
